title: De novo design of orthogonal far-red; orange; and green fluorophore-binding proteins for multiplexed imaging.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed all files in the two Zenodo deposits for this paper: a 17.4 GB code archive (same content as github.com/steffen-klein/novotag-design) and a ~31 GB 'Raw data' deposit of 14 per-figure zips (CC-BY-4.0). Downloaded the smallest zip (Fig_S16.zip, 2.1 MB compressed) and found 4 microscopy/gel TIFF images in panel folders, no table. Listed the full GitHub tree (8,527 files, 1.5 GB) and downloaded the only result tables in it: df_all_results.csv (144 rows x 34 columns), df_all_results_filtered.csv (46 rows), df_orig_pdb.csv (11 rows) - all columns are computed design metrics (AlphaFold2 pLDDT/PAE/RMSD, RoseTTAFold2 all-atom scores). Opened the preprint supplement PDF (2 pages: crystallography statistics and a 4-row Rosetta table). Searched Zenodo, DataCite and the Sequence Read Archive for any screening dataset: nothing. Confirmed PDB entry 9PVL (one crystal structure) exists.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The experimental screen itself: 6,032 / 5,800 / 4,843 designs tested per dye (JF657/JF596/JF494) and 334 JF657 binders enriched at 5 micromolar or better. These numbers come from the bioRxiv preprint methods text (bioRxiv 2025.08.03.668343, PMC12424662); no file containing those designs or their outcomes was found anywhere.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked the files: the only deposits are raw microscopy images (~31 GB of per-figure TIFF zips) and a code archive. The labelled screening data (designs plus yeast-display sorting/sequencing outcomes) is described in the methods but deposited nowhere - no Sequence Read Archive accession, no Zenodo table, supplement is two crystallography tables.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked the files: no column anywhere holds a measured binding outcome. The label (binder / non-binder, or the concentration at which half the yeast cells are collected) would have to be reconstructed from fluorescence-activated cell sorting and MiSeq read counts that were never released.

a3_inputs_present.note: Amino acid sequences are present as a column in the three small CSVs I opened, and design PDB coordinate files are in the repository, so inputs would not need identifier lookups.

a4_units_stated.note: Columns in the 144-row table are unitless model scores with self-describing names (af2_plddt, af2_rmsd_usalign in angstroms, rf2aa_mean_protein_ligand_pae); images are TIFFs with no measurement units needed.

a5_enough_rows.note: Counted in the file: df_all_results.csv has 144 split-variant designs (46 after the authors' filter) built from 11 parent designs. Far below the ~400 minimum for classification; the ~16,675 screened designs exist only as sentences in the methods.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 0.3 MB of tables (the ~31 GB image deposit would not be used)
a6_fits_laptop.note: The three CSVs total under 0.4 MB and load instantly; the image deposit is 31 GB and would fail this check if it were the working set.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked: the paper's 6,032 / 5,800 / 4,843 design counts have no corresponding file, so there is nothing to reconcile. The 144 rows in the repository table are example pipeline output, not a reported figure.

a8_label_provenance.note: Checked the files: every candidate label in the only table is another model's output (AlphaFold2 pLDDT and predicted aligned error, RoseTTAFold2 all-atom binding probability, structural RMSD to the design model). Training on these distills AlphaFold2, not biology.

existing_models.name: AlphaFold2-based binder design filter (Bennett et al. 2023, Nature Communications, 'Improving de novo protein binder design with deep learning')
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported roughly a 10-fold increase in experimental design success rate when AlphaFold2 interface predictions are used to filter designs, judged against yeast-display sorting; I read the abstract and a search summary only, not the paper, and did not verify code or weight availability.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not verified - I did not retrieve the discussion section.

existing_models.name: Machine-learning binder design plus high-throughput display comparison (Yao et al. 2026, Protein Science; mRNA display versus yeast surface display)
existing_models.score_and_split: Screened 2,009 designs against TLT-1 and 3,159 against B7-H3 across two display formats and reported that dual enrichment predicts binder function; numbers come from the search summary of the abstract, not from opening the paper.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) with LigandMPNN or AlphaFold2 scores as extra features
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would suffice for ~17,000 short (40-120 residue) sequences, if the sequences and their screening outcomes existed
backbone.licence: ESM-2 weights are MIT-licensed; the paper's code archive on GitHub carries no licence file, and the Zenodo image deposit is CC-BY-4.0

integration.partner_dataset: Other published de novo binder screens with released sorting data (for example the mini-binder yeast-display campaigns from the same lab) joined on amino acid sequence
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a model of which designed small-molecule binders actually bind transfer across target ligands and design campaigns - a question that cannot be asked here because this campaign's outcomes were never deposited.

controls.positive_control: Would be: recover the known effect that higher shape complementarity and lower Rosetta binding energy enrich for real binders; not runnable, no measured outcomes released.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling on the 144-row table is possible but meaningless, since those labels are AlphaFold2 and RoseTTAFold2 scores.
controls.external_validation: None available from this paper; one crystal structure (PDB 9PVL) and a handful of purified-protein binding curves shown in figures only.

honest_claim_h3: With what is actually public, a model could only claim to reproduce AlphaFold2 and RoseTTAFold2 confidence scores for 144 split variants of 11 designed proteins - a restatement of those models, not a statement about whether a designed protein binds a dye.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a designed protein's sequence and modelled structure to predict whether it really binds its target dye in the lab.
plain_idea.train_on: Intended: each of the ~16,675 computer-designed mini-proteins (sequence, modelled complex with the dye, physics-based interface scores) tested against the three Janelia Fluor dyes. In reality only 144 designs with purely computational scores are public.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a design is enriched as a binder in yeast surface display, and at roughly what affinity; the true answer comes from fluorescence-activated cell sorting followed by deep sequencing of the sorted pools - data this paper never deposited.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Protein designers currently throw away thousands of designs using hand-tuned structural filters; a model trained on real screen outcomes would tell them which filters matter and cut synthesis costs. Even a failure would quantify how little the current filters predict.

more_or_better_data.why: The paper's 16,675 screened designs would be a genuinely useful addition to the handful of published design-success screens, but none of it is public; what is public is 144 rows of model scores.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements and no measured values of any kind are released, so per-prediction uncertainty cannot be calibrated against anything.

models_beatable.why: The AlphaFold2-score filtering approach (Bennett et al. 2023) is a heuristic threshold rather than a trained success classifier, so it would be beatable - but only with screening outcome data that does not exist here.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition outright: there is no feature/label table to train or evaluate on, so neither a baseline run nor a shared split is possible.

ml_idea: Intended project: predict experimental binding success (yeast-display enrichment, and the concentration at which half the displaying cells are collected) for de novo designed dye-binding mini-proteins from sequence plus modelled complex features, using a frozen protein language model with a small head, and ask whether success predictors transfer across the three chemically similar dyes. The project is not executable because the screen's design sequences and outcomes were not deposited; the only public tables hold 144 designs labelled with AlphaFold2 and RoseTTAFold2 scores, which would distill those models rather than learn binding.

effort.compute_note: Estimates cover only the three tiny CSVs I actually downloaded (under 0.4 MB); no estimate is possible for the intended task because the screening table does not exist. The 31 GB image deposit was deliberately not downloaded beyond one 2.1 MB zip.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask: is there a single file anywhere with one row per designed protein and a measured binding outcome? Listing the two Zenodo deposits and the GitHub tree answers no in ten minutes, which is exactly what happened.

verdict_reason: The labelled dataset the project needs - 16,675 designs with yeast-display binding outcomes - was never deposited (A1, A2, A7). The only public tables hold 144 designs whose columns are AlphaFold2 and RoseTTAFold2 scores (A5, A8); the rest is ~31 GB of raw microscopy images and a code archive.
